newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Burford aims to keep outperforming.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Burford aims to keep outperforming.

text.p: Burford Holdings Plc's chief executive Nick Leslau said on Thursday the group aimed to continue outperforming the British property sector.
Asked if Burford could continue to perform better than the rest of the market, Leslau told Reuters "If our track record is anything to go by then hopefully we will".
Earlier Burford announced increased pre-tax profits of 15.06 million stg for 1996, up from 11.16 million in 1995. Net asset value (NAV) per share rose to 110.1 pence from 101.5 pence.
"We've made it clear that the day we can't outperform the market we'll sell the company," Leslau said. Burford's NAV per shareholder rose by 21 percent to 122.9 pence in 1996.
This included free shares from the demergers during 1996 of Grantchester and Columbus. Burford's chairman Nigel Wray said in his results statement that this summed up the group's philosophy.

"This in a nutshell is the very simple philosophy of Burford - to sensibly increase NAV per share by the maximum possible amount and to see the highest possible share price for shareholders always, we hope, with an eagle eye on the downside," Wray said.
He said that while his dual role as both chief executive of Burford and the dynamic Trocadero kept him "incredibly busy", it was not a distraction from his work at Burford.

But once Trocadero, which demerged from Burford in 1995, moves from the junior Alternative Investment Market (AIM) onto London's main stock market its regulations would in any case mean would no longer be allowed to be its chief executive.
Leslau said while pursuing other avenues, he would stick with property as his main area of interest, adding that Burford was working on numerous deals.

He said Burford was working on a joint venture with an established hotels operator to set up "lifestyle hotels" in central London. He said Burford had already bought four properties for this, including one in Soho.

Leslau said Burford's current gearing of only 41 percent meant the group had plenty of scope for further acquisitions before it reached its self-imposed 100 percent gearing level. "We've got 275 million pounds of buying power," he said.
Burford announced an increased total dividend of 2.1 pence per share. Its shares were down 2.5 pence at 142.5 pence at 0930 GMT.
